description: We don't just think outside the box. We debug the box, rewrite it, and build something better. A team of coders ready to take on the universe, one challenge at a time.
summary: For the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge ("Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map"), we developed Marswalk HUD—an immersive, first-person astronaut helmet interface designed to plan and execute Marswalks on the Martian surface. Rather than relying on traditional top-down 2D maps, our application merges real NASA rover panoramas (Perseverance Mastcam-Z) with a sci-fi visor overlay that tracks critical life-support metrics—including Oxygen, Battery, Comms, and Radiation. Users can click directly on the 360° terrain to drop waypoints, dynamically calculating route distance, solar recharge trade-offs, and ridge-line communication blackouts in real-time. This project addresses the challenge by fusing geological target acquisition, hazard avoidance, and rigorous life-support constraints into a human-centric navigation tool. It is vital because it transforms raw mission telemetry and rover data into an intuitive, cinematic, and functional experience that mirrors what real explorers need on Mars.
details: What it does & How it works Marswalk HUD is a web-based, first-person astronaut helmet simulation. It renders a 360° equirectangular Martian panorama (Gediz Vallis) using Pannellum. As astronauts or mission planners pan across the landscape and click on the terrain, custom vector mathematics and spherical trigonometry calculate exact surface distances between waypoints. Each movement dynamically triggers trade-off logic: traversing into direct sunlight provides solar battery recharge bonuses but increases radiation exposure, while moving behind ridges cuts off communication lines. The helmet HUD reflects these updates instantly across live resource bars, a mini-map radar with target blips, telemetry readouts, and interactive mineral sample data cards. Intended Impact & Benefits The project bridges the gap between complex NASA science data and practical surface operations. By giving explorers an interactive preview of a route's oxygen and power consumption before committing to a trek, it prevents mission-critical failures and highlights high-priority science targets (such as hydrated silica and delta sediment layers). Tech Stack & Tools Used Frontend Core: Vanilla JavaScript, HTML5, and CSS3 styled with a custom sci-fi visor layout (Orbitron and Share Tech Mono typography). Panorama Engine: Pannellum 360° viewer library loaded via CDN. Data & Logic: Structured scene JSON architecture incorporating real NASA/JPL-Caltech Perseverance Mastcam-Z data, custom vector route-planning mathematics, and a synchronized HUD state controller. Creativity & Design Considerations Instead of a standard flat map, our team focused heavily on human-centric, cinematic immersion—replicating an authentic EVA helmet experience complete with a boot sequence, warning alerts for high radiation, audio support structures, and seamless coordination between infrastructure, UI design, route math, and science datasets.
